_comment: The shared secret-masking ruleset, as data.
PLAN.md Section 25 lists this as a Build Once Contract with four call
sites: the native adapter, legacy stdout, credential handling, and the
Ansible callback bridge. The last of those is Python, which is why this
is a JSON file rather than a Go slice: one artifact, read by both
languages, so the two halves cannot drift.
HONEST STATUS: the Python half does not exist yet. Phase 22 ships this
file, the Go embed, and the COPY into the legacy runner image. Phase 25
writes the callback plugin that reads it. Saying the ruleset is applied
in Go and Python today would be a false claim, so this comment says so
instead.
There is deliberately no rule kind for a literal secret VALUE. A value
worth masking is never known at build time and must never be committed
to a file, so runtime values travel through redact.Literals instead.
That is the third channel, and it is code rather than data on purpose.
Each pattern rule carries a prefilter and samples. The prefilter is a set
of cheap lowercase substrings, at least one of which any match must
contain; a line containing none of them skips the regex entirely, which is
what keeps masking off the critical path of every log line. The samples are
strings the rule MUST mask. They exist because a wrong prefilter would
silently disable its own rule, and a silently disabled masking rule is the
worst failure this file has available: the tests assert every sample both
passes its prefilter and is actually masked, so the prefilter cannot drift
away from the pattern it guards.
A pattern rule with secret_groups masks only its capturing groups and keeps
the rest of the match, and keeps a group that already holds a placeholder
(this file's ******** or pkg/netcfg's pleiades-masked-). The SNMP rules use
it so a configuration line still says which keyword its secret followed.
The Python half must honor it as well.

rules.name: credential_field_names
rules.description: Structured-log attribute names whose value is a secret by construction, an SNMP credential's community and passphrases among them, by their flattened key (snmp_community) and the passphrases by their pleiades_snmp input id (auth_passphrase). A bare community is deliberately not one: a name matches by any run of its words, and BGP communities are not secrets, so community_entries in a parsed show bgp summary, or a bgp_community variable, would be refused as facts and never copied from a playbook. A key rule is only applicable where the attribute name is still visible, which is inside slog.HandlerOptions.ReplaceAttr and nowhere else. This is the concrete reason the ordering constraint on the logging seam exists.

rules.name: ansible_credential_field_names
rules.description: The same rule for Ansible's own variable names, which appear as attribute keys once the legacy adapter's inventory and callback output are logged.

rules.name: pem_private_key
rules.description: A PEM private key block, in any of its forms (RSA, EC, OPENSSH, PKCS8). Secret by construction: no PEM private key is ever safe to print, whether or not this process knows it is a credential. The (?s) flag lets the dot cross the newlines a PEM block always contains, and the lazy .*? stops at the first END line so two adjacent keys do not merge into one match.
samples:
-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIBOgIBAAJBAK
-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----

-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----
b3BlbnNzaC1rZXk
-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----

rules.name: bearer_token
rules.description: An HTTP Authorization bearer token, which reaches a log whenever a request header is dumped. Matches the scheme word too, so the masked output shows that authorization was present without showing what it was.

rules.name: json_web_token
rules.description: A JWT. The eyJ prefix is the base64url encoding of the opening of every JOSE header, so this is distinctive enough to carry almost no false-positive risk, and a JWT in a log line is a session anybody reading that line can replay.

rules.name: aws_access_key_id
rules.description: An AWS access key identifier, across the documented resource-type prefixes. The matching secret access key is deliberately NOT a pattern rule: it is 40 characters of base64 with no distinguishing prefix, so a pattern for it would scrub unrelated hashes, git object ids and base64 payloads out of every log line in the system. That value is covered by the literal channel instead, where its exact bytes are known.

rules.name: url_userinfo
rules.description: Credentials embedded in a URL, the shape a database DSN or a git remote takes. The match includes the scheme, so the masked output loses the scheme along with the credentials. That is accepted rather than worked around: RE2 has no lookbehind, so matching the userinfo alone is not expressible, and a replacement template that reassembled the surviving parts would be a place to get a leak wrong.

rules.name: snmp_community
rules.description: An SNMPv1/v2c community in a device's configuration: an IOS or NX-OS snmp-server community line, a net-snmp rocommunity or rwcommunity line and their IPv6 forms, or the trapcommunity a net-snmp agent sends its traps with. A community is a password sent in the clear, and one shorter than eight characters is masked by this shape alone, since masking it by value would scrub ordinary words from every output.

rules.name: snmp_com2sec_community
rules.description: The community a net-snmp com2sec line maps to a security name, its third argument after any -Cn context.

rules.name: snmp_server_host_community
rules.description: The community an IOS or NX-OS snmp-server host line sends its notifications with, after the address and any vrf, traps or informs and version 1 or 2c. With version 3 the word there is a USM user, not a secret, and an NX-OS use-vrf, filter-vrf or source-interface line holds no community, so each of those matches without a group and masks nothing.
samples: snmp-server host 192.0.2.1 vrf Mgmt-intf informs version 2c c0mmunity-s3cret
snmp-server host 10.0.0.1 traps version 2c public udp-port 162

rules.name: snmp_net_snmp_trap_community
rules.description: The community a net-snmp agent's trapsink, trap2sink or informsink line sends to its host with, its second argument, and the community an snmptrapd authCommunity line accepts, after its types.

rules.name: snmp_net_snmp_trapsess_community
rules.description: The community a net-snmp trapsess line passes as -c, apart or attached. The option is matched in lower case only, since snmpcmd reads -C as another option.

rules.name: snmp_net_snmp_trapsess_auth_passphrase
rules.description: The authentication passphrase a net-snmp trapsess line passes as -A, apart or attached. The option is matched in upper case only, since -a names the protocol.
samples: trapsess -v 3 -u monitor -l authPriv -a SHA -A auth-pass-7 -x AES -X priv-pass-7 10.0.0.1

rules.name: snmp_net_snmp_trapsess_priv_passphrase
rules.description: The privacy passphrase a net-snmp trapsess line passes as -X, apart or attached, in upper case only, since -x names the protocol. It is its own rule so a line naming -X before -A is masked too.
samples: trapsess -v 3 -u monitor -l authPriv -X priv-pass-8 -a SHA -A auth-pass-8 10.0.0.1

rules.name: snmp_v3_user_passphrases
rules.description: An IOS or NX-OS SNMPv3 user's authentication and privacy passphrases, or its localized keys, each after its algorithm: IOS's sha-2 256 and aes 128, NX-OS's sha-256 and aes-128, and NX-OS's priv with no algorithm, which is DES. IOS does not print these in its running configuration and NX-OS prints the localized keys, so this is for a line an operator or a runbook wrote, echoed back, and for an NX-OS running configuration.
samples: snmp-server user monitor grp v3 auth sha auth-pass-1 priv aes 256 priv-pass-1
snmp-server user monitor grp v3 auth sha-2 512 auth-pass-2 priv 3des priv-pass-2 access 10
snmp-server user monitor grp v3 encrypted auth md5 0a1b2c3d4e5f
snmp-server user admin network-admin auth sha-256 auth-pass-9 priv aes-128 priv-pass-9
snmp-server user admin network-admin auth md5 0x1a2b3c4d priv 0x5e6f7a8b localizedkey

rules.name: snmp_net_snmp_create_user
rules.description: A net-snmp createUser line's authentication passphrase and, when it has one of its own, its privacy passphrase, each after its algorithm and either a word or a double-quoted phrase.
samples: createUser monitor SHA auth-pass-4 AES priv-pass-4
createUser -e 0x8000000001020304 monitor SHA-256 "auth pass five" AES-256 "priv pass five"
